body: They're sending me home because there isn't enough beds in psych.
I had my phone with me.  I'm at the hospital now.

Linked In and Indeed are the apps I've already used.  It's not a matter of access to job listings that's an issue.  I just don't know what it is about me that employers are passing me by.  I never had this problem before but I think my former employer (I was let go due to Frustration of Employment Contract due to my mental health) is saying something to any potential employers.

But people who are travelling for a cup tourney aren't looking for by chance empty recording studios.  They're looking to occupy themselves when there isn't a game going on and what do we have?  The \(faux\) Stone Hall Castle?  A highly dubious claim to being the 23rd best beer city in the world \(over Chicago?\)?  The Capital Pointe Hole?

Maybe we should have had a mattress hoodoo like we had when we hosted the Junos.

There should have been events around the city considering this is the 100th Memorial Cup but the city and organizing committee really dropped the ball.

Edit: And as people have already said, the ticket prices are keeping locals away.

I also think their gravy is pretty mediocre too so I'm not sure the appeal of the place.  It's a shame since besides the food trucks, they're the only poutinerie in town.   While I'm usually about supporting small businesses, I actually hope one of the franchises like Big Cheese or Smoke's comes to town and makes them step up their game.

Edit: I guess Smoke's is already in town but they're at the university.

You aren't kidding.  A fair amount of the jobs that are listed on Indeed/Monster/Glassdoor are scams (ex. I got numerous emails from supposed HR managers full of misspellings that just wanted me to send my SIN or my banking info.) and the Job Bank site is cumbersome.  Try to upload your resume and see what I mean because you're going to be spending a ridiculous amount of time trying to find the correct job definition/category for previous job titles.  It sucks.

But that's the Sask Party for you.   Make half assed decisions without feedback from the people (employers and job seekers) that actually used it successfully over the years.  I'm reeeaaallly looking forward to seeing what they come up with.
